title: Buying a ukulele as a boy
summary: At eleven or twelve he shined shoes and sold papers to save $2.50 for a ukulele and taught himself from an instruction book.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Tell us about your first interest in music. When you were a little boy, did you start on any instrument?

Well, when I was a small boy, Bill, I became intrigued with a ukulele I saw in a small place on Orleans between Johnson and Preah called Miss Campanelle. And which incidentally, that place is still there right now. And I just sold papers and shined shoes and did everything I could to get that uke. And I didn't have it over two or three weeks with an instruction book that I could play it pretty well, just to entertain the gang on the street at night. But I never had in my mind that one day that would be the start of a musical career for me.
How old were you about when you got there?

Oh, I was about eleven or twelve. I was shining shoes around here and I got that ukulele. I played a, in other words, a convention came to town. And, of course, the ukulele didn't cost but two and a half, but trying to get two and a half them days was rough. And I went up there and shined shoes so my fingers was to the bone. But I finally got that two and a half and bought that ukulele.
